requiredRuntimeSemantics: The predicate must observe a committed corpse consumption event associated with the Necropolis law owner side.
The consumed corpse source must be correlated to a successful raise, drain, curse, or Night death spell after spell classification has passed.
Cooldown mutation may only use the event once, after consumption is committed and before duplicate spell or UI preview paths can fire.

corpse count read counted as committed consumption
undead unit identity counted as consumed corpse
spell classification counted without corpse consumption
spellbook preview or hover counted as consumption
generic death event counted as consumed corpse
temporary summoned loss counted as consumed corpse

requiredRuntimeSemantics: The predicate must read a logical corpse count from a defined battle, site, or side-scoped corpse state source.
The corpse count must be captured at the law packet's intended timing before temporary mana is granted and later cleaned up.
Corpse count, affected hero, battle context, and Necropolis law owner must all correlate before any temporary resource mutation.

undead unit count counted as corpse count
temporary summoned loss counted as corpse count
generic casualty count counted as corpse count without corpse-production policy
dead stack animation counted as corpse count

requiredRuntimeSemantics: The predicate must identify an explicit corpse site, recent battle site, corpse-rich location, graveyard, or undead-dwelling object/state source.
Reveal targets must come from exact object allowlists or proven corpse/battle-site state, not from visual corpse art.
Object or site identity, reveal radius origin, target side, and Necropolis law owner must correlate before fog reveal mutation is allowed.

requiredRuntimeSemantics: The predicate must observe either committed corpse consumption or a committed raise event that consumes a corpse-equivalent resource.
The event must be correlated to the Necropolis law owner and to the Death Moon calendar timing before Astrology progress or pressure effects are granted.
Raise/corpse consumption must be idempotent across battle result, spell result, and calendar refresh paths.

raise-capable spell classification counted without committed raise or corpse consumption
corpse availability counted as raise consumption

generic kill or casualty event counted as consumed corpse
